[MUQATIL:19:93-95/r1] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | All in the heavens and earth, including angels, ʿUzayr, Jesus, Mary, and others, come to the Merciful as servants who acknowledge servitude to him.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p247/r3] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | Every creature in heaven and earth comes to the Merciful as a servant, counted and alone on Judgment Day, as in another verse. | mentions 6:94
[AZRAQI:v1p179/r1] AZRAQI, d. 249 · أبو صالح مولى أم هاني | reports | The passage enumerates Quraysh and a broad set of Arab groups, including Kināna, Khuzāʿa, Aws and Khazraj, Thaqīf, Ghatafān, ʿAdwān, and Quḍāʿa.
[AZRAQI:v1p179/r2] AZRAQI, d. 249 · قريش | reports | When Quraysh married a woman from another Arab group, they stipulated that any children she bore would be Ahmasī and follow Quraysh's religion.
[AZRAQI:v1p179/r3] AZRAQI, d. 249 · قريش | reports | As an example, Quraysh married al-Adram Taim ibn Ghalib to Majd, daughter of Taim Rabīʿa ibn ʿĀmir, on the condition that their children follow Quraysh's Ahmasī practice.
[AZRAQI:v1p179/r4] AZRAQI, d. 249 · لبيد بن ربيعة بن جعفر الكلابي | reports | The source cites Labīd's verse naming Majd, Numayr, and the tribes of Hilāl in a line about his people and their watering.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r1] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · الأصمعي | reports | Al-Aṣmaʿī and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar did not know Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt’s verse likening earth to a female for rain; later interpreters explain rain makes the earth bear vegetation.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r2] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · author | holds | The verse’s imagery treats earth as female and rain as male, which fertilizes it; the same pairing is applied to firesticks, whose spark is their offspring.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r3] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · author | holds | مسفد means mated: the male si fada the female, and God caused him to mate, parallel to nakaha/ankahahu.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r4] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · ذو الرمة | reports | In Dhu al-Rumma’s parallel verse, السقط means fire, the father is the upper firestick, and the mother is the lower firestick.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r5] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · الأصمعي | reports | A second Umayya poem was transmitted as عسل ما, but the author says it should read سلع ما; al-Salʿ and al-ʿUshr are trees used in rain-making rites by tying and burning them on cows’ tails.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r6] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · author | holds | وعالت البيقورا means a drought year burdened the cows with the ritual branches and fire; al-ʿāʾil means poor, and a second poet’s verse supports the corrected reading سلع.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r7] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · الأصمعي | reports | Al-Aṣmaʿī said the learned had disappeared who could explain Imruʾ al-Qays’s verse about سلكى and مخلوجة.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r8] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · author | reports | The source continues al-Aṣmaʿī’s report, saying likewise that no one remained who understood al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza’s verse about those who struck the ʿayr.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r1] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · الأصمعي | reports | Al-Aṣmaʿī reads سلكى as a straight stab and مخلوجة as one veering right or left, like two arrows that do not land alike.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r10] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · ابن الأعرابي | reports | Ibn al-Aʿrābī says منغمس في الأهيغين means absorbed in eating and sex; the two الأطيبان likewise mean food and sex.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r11] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · ابن الأعرابي | reports | Ibn al-Aʿrābī explains that a sword blow left the bull’s side hanging as it leaned; خذع means inclination.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r2] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · زيد بن كثوة العنبري | reports | Zayd says people misquote the line: it is كر كلامين على نابل, two stabs delivered without pause, like telling an archer twice to shoot; he prefers this sense.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r3] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · بعضهم | reports | One view makes العير a tent peg, named for its protrusion like the raised middle of an arrowhead; the line blames the group for every tent-dweller’s offense.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r4] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · بعضهم | reports | Another view identifies العير with Kulaib Waʾil, the chief, deriving the title from the onager as the largest wild animal.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r5] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · رسول الله | reports | The Prophet told Abu Sufyan, «كل الصيد في جوف العير», a report used to support العير as the greatest beast.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r6] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · آخر | reports | A further view makes العير a mountain near Medina and invokes the Prophet’s prohibition of the area between ʿAyr and Thawr; the line implicates anyone reaching that place.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r7] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · آخر | reports | Another interpretation takes العير literally as a donkey: the group is blamed for the offenses of everyone who drives one.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r8] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · author | holds | Ibn Qutayba sums up the views: the speakers are saddled with everyone’s sins and treated as their allies.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r9] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · الأصمعي | reports | Al-Aṣmaʿī cannot determine two phrases by Ruʾba: the line about الأهيغ seems to imply water, and he also does not know كأنه حامل جنب أخذعا.
[TAB-FULL:v15p639#2/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | All angels, humans, and jinn will come to God on Judgment Day as His humbled servants, affirming their servitude and having no kinship with Him.
[TAB-FULL:v15p639#2/r6] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Ātī is an active participle from the verb ataytuhu, meaning I came to him.
[NAHHAS:v3p29/r3] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | The written yāʾ in ātin reflects an original tanwīn that was omitted for ease and then annexed.
[IBNHIBBAN:v8p118/r1] IBNHIBBAN, d. 354 · أبو ذر | reports | Abū Dharr reports the Prophet’s warning against hoarding: he would give away even a mountain of gold, the wealthy will be few on Judgment Day, and monotheists enter Paradise even if they sinned.
[IBNHIBBAN:v8p118/r2] IBNHIBBAN, d. 354 · أبو حاتم | holds | Abū Ḥātim says the promise is conditional: God may pardon a monotheist’s sins before entry, or the person may enter after punishment in Hell; it is not an unconditional guarantee.
[SULAMI:v1p433#2/r1] SULAMI, d. 412 · أبو بكر الوراق | reports | The finest approach to God is constant servanthood and confessed need: servanthood sustains service, and need sustains refuge and humble pleading.
[SULAMI:v1p433#2/r2] SULAMI, d. 412 · جعفر بن محمد | reports | The one who comes to the Merciful as a servant is poor and humbled by his own qualities, or noble by pointing through the qualities of the Real.
[THALABI:v6p232/r1] THALABI, d. 427 · أبو هريرة | reports | In a divine report, God says the servant falsely denies resurrection and slanders Him by claiming He has taken a child, then affirms divine oneness. | mentions 112:1, 112:3
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p338#2/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | Those in heaven are angels and those on earth are creatures; each comes to God as a lowly, submissive servant.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p338#2/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | All creation are God’s servants, including Jesus and ʿUzayr.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p338#2/r6] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The word ʿabdan is accusative as a circumstantial expression (ḥāl).
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:90-97/r4] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | Every creature in the heavens and earth will come to God on Judgment Day admitting servitude to him.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r1] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | Fronted مثل need not refer to a second person: it can mean that anyone matching the addressee in quality would naturally act or refrain as described.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r2] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | The reply to al-Ḥajjāj’s threat exploits مثل الأمير to comment on what an emir’s rank or customary conduct entails, not to refer to another person.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r3] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | Likewise, غيري can mean I am not among those who are deceived or ungrateful; it does not necessarily identify and disparage another person.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r4] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | Abū Tammām’s غيري verse denies that he is ungrateful and base; Jurjānī says it cannot be an accusation that another poet committed the offense.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r5] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | Using مثل and غير this way is rooted in ordinary instinct and established usage.
[DAMGHANI:v1p15/r2] DAMGHANI, d. 478 · author | holds | Atā can mean acknowledge and submit: every creature comes to the Merciful acknowledging servitude.
[MUALLAQAT:v1p189#4/r1] MUALLAQAT, d. 486 · author | holds | Al-Zawzanī explains the line as a cow fearing that either space between her legs may be the locus of danger, so she cannot tell which way to flee.
[MUALLAQAT:v1p189#4/r2] MUALLAQAT, d. 486 · author | holds | Al-Zawzanī says كلا is singular in form but dual in sense, while كل is singular in form despite its collective sense; 19:93 illustrates agreement by form, alongside 18:33 and 27:87 as contrasts. | mentions 18:33, 27:87, 19:93
[MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r1] MUALLAQAT, d. 486 · author | holds | The poet reports a sweeping claim that everyone who performs the act under discussion is their ally, then says he is their ally; al-Zawzanī says the line's ending has the same sense under every reading of العير.
[MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r2] MUALLAQAT, d. 486 · author | reports | If العير means a lord, the claim is that all who approve killing Kalib b. Wa'il are their cousins and the blood-feuds attach to the poet's group as allies.
[MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r3] MUALLAQAT, d. 486 · author | reports | If العير means a wild ass, all hunters of wild asses are called their allies, extending the guilt of a particular group to the public.
[MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r4] MUALLA
<<part 0 ends; continues in part 1>>

QAT, d. 486 · author | reports | If العير means a tent peg, everyone who pitches tents is called their ally, extending one group's guilt to the Arabs at large.
[MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r5] MUALLAQAT, d. 486 · author | reports | If العير means a mote, everyone who stirs motes aside to clear water is called their ally.
[MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r6] MUALLAQAT, d. 486 · author | reports | If العير means a particular mountain, everyone who reaches that mountain is called their ally.
[JISHUMI:v6p4621/r6] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Servanthood and sonship cannot coexist; if a man owned his son, the son would be emancipated.
[JISHUMI:v6p4621/r7] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Every being coming to God as a servant negates divine offspring, since God is not a body and offspring is a property of bodies.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r3] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Every being in the heavens and earth will come to the Merciful as a humbled, submissive servant; all creation belongs to Him.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p48#2/r1] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Man after kull is adjectival because kull is indefinite, as in a poetic example where rabb is likewise followed by man.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r10] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · ابن مسعود | reports | Ibn Masʿūd reads “He wrote them down and counted them.”
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r11] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · أبي | reports | Ubayy's codex reads “He counted them and enumerated them completely.”
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r12] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Arriving alone conveys little support or strength, with no protector from God's will.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r22] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The verse may connect to the preceding account of everyone coming as servant and alone: God comforts believers through love shown in honor, gifts, and signs of forgiveness.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Inna is negative, equivalent to mā; the common reading annexes “coming” to the Merciful.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · طلحة بن مصرف | reports | Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif reads ātin with tanwīn and the following noun in the accusative.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · ابن مسعود | reports | Ibn Masʿūd reads lammā atā al-Raḥmān.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · بعض الناس | reports | Some infer that a child cannot be a servant; the author calls this inference remote.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r8] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | ʿAbdan is an accusative of state.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r9] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | God encompasses and knows His servants; enumeration is stated and restated in different words, while ʿaddan emphasizes the action.
[TABRISI:19:93-96/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Lidd means intense contentiousness; the cited verse and poem illustrate the word and its plural form. | mentions 2:204
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p165/r1] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | Ityān is the verbal noun of atā, meaning to come; ātā with a long vowel means to give, and the camel’s form istāʾtat describes seeking a mate.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p165/r8] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · بعض المفسرين | reports | A seventh sense is acknowledgment: every being comes to the Merciful admitting servitude to Him.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p265#3/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | Everyone in heaven and earth will come to God on Judgment Day as a humble servant, including Jesus, Ezra, and the angels.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p265#3/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · القاضي أبو يعلى | reports | Abu Yaʿla infers that a parent who buys his own child no longer owns him, since purchase emancipates him: sonship and enslavement cannot coexist.
[RAZI-FULL:v21p217#2/r8] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Every worshipped being in heaven and earth, including angels and people, returns to God as a submissive, humble servant who hopes in Him.
[RAZI-FULL:v21p217#2/r9] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · بعضهم | reports | Some restrict the statement about every being coming as a servant to the Day of Judgment; Razi prefers the unrestricted reading because it needs no restriction.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:93#2/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The discussion had appeared under al-Baqara and elsewhere; repeating it here is appropriate.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | “In” is negative: everyone in heaven and earth will come on Judgment Day acknowledging God’s lordship in submission, as in 27:87; all are His servants, so none can be His child. | mentions 27:87
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | “Ātī” is written with yāʾ; its original tanwīn is dropped for ease and the form is annexed.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The verse proves a parent cannot own a child: God contrasts sonship with servitude, which cannot coexist; if a father cannot own his son, the son cannot own his father all the more.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | The sound Muslim report says a child cannot repay a parent except by finding the parent enslaved, buying him, and freeing him.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · إسحاق بن راهويه | reports | Isḥāq ibn Rāhwayh interprets emancipation of a share in a slave as referring only to male slaves, so freeing a share in a female would not complete emancipation.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الجمهور | reports | The majority reject Isḥāq’s distinction and include male and female slaves, since “ʿabd” is generic and this verse encompasses both.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | A divine saying transmitted by al-Bukhārī through Abū Hurayra says Adam’s son falsely denies resurrection and insults God by claiming He has a child, though He is One and has no offspring or equal.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:19:93-96/r1] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Every being in the heavens and earth belongs to the Merciful and approaches Him as a servant in submission; one reading preserves the original form of the verb.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | إن كل من is an indefinite noun described by the following phrase; its predicate is إلا آتي الرحمن. The singular participle and pronoun agree with the lexical form of كل; it is an active participle in future sense.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | عبدا is a circumstantial accusative meaning submissive, lowly, and obedient; all angels and humans come before God on Judgment Day admitting servitude.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Servitude and sonship are incompatible: all are attributed to God as servants; even ownership of one's child would emancipate the child, so some cannot be children while others are servants.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r4] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · ابن مسعود | reports | Ibn Masud reads آت الرحمن in its original form before annexation.
[QASHANI:19:93-95/r1] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | All in heaven and earth come as servants because possible beings have no existence or perfection apart from divine effusion through Rahman; they remain governed and compelled under His dominion.
[QASHANI:19:93-95/r2] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | Their primordial readiness worships God so they may exist; after existence they owe worship by fulfilling the rights of His gifts to become complete.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | prefers | Abu Hayyan prefers taking من after كل as a relative pronoun meaning all who are in the heavens and earth.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari instead calls من a descriptive indefinite after كل, by analogy with its occurrence after رب.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · عبد الله وابن الزبير وأبو حيوة وطلحة وأبو بحرية وابن أبي عبلة ويعقوب | reports | These readers recite إلا آت with nunation and الرحمن in the accusative; the majority read it in a genitive construction, and آتي is the predicate of كل with عبدا circumstantial.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Repeating الرحمن emphasizes that no one else deserves this name, since the origins and branches of blessings come from Him.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The beings claimed as deities, including angels, Jesus, and Ezra, all come to the Merciful as obedient servants; alleged filial status cannot confer divinity.
[SAMIN-DURR:19:93/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · عبد الله بن الزبير وأبو حيوة وطلحة | reports | They and others read آتي with tanwin and الرحمن in the accusative; the majority use annexation.
[SAMIN-DURR:19:93/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | عبدا and فردا are circumstantial accusatives.
[SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء والزمخشري | reports | They take من في السماوات as an indefinite noun qualified by the following prepositional phrase; their wording appears to exclude other parses.
[SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الشيخ | reports | من may instead be relative, with كل applying to a generic relative noun; it must be universal rather than one known person. | mentions 39:33
[SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The poetic كل الذي حملتني supports the relative analysis; the relative must be interpreted universally for كل to be annexed to it.
[SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | آتي الرحمن is the predicate of كل, singular by its form; plural would also be possible when agreement follows meaning.
[SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · السهيلي | reports | Al-Suhayli says clause-initial كل annexed to a definite should take a singular predicate, understood as كل واحد; the Sheikh requires Arabic attestation for plural agreement.
[SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The author corrects the terminology: singular agreement follows the word's form, while plural follows meaning; Qurani

[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p267/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | God has counted every creature, male and female, young and old, from creation until Resurrection.
[BURHAN:v1p13/r1] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | Tafsir is the knowledge of understanding God’s revealed Book, explaining its meanings, and deriving its rulings and wisdom; it draws on language, grammar, morphology, rhetoric, legal theory, and readings, and requires knowledge of revelation contexts and abrogation.
[BURHAN:v1p13/r2] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | Exegetical works reflect their authors’ strongest fields: al-Zajjaj and al-Wahidi emphasize rare vocabulary, al-Tha‘labi stories, al-Zamakhshari rhetoric, and Fakhr al-Din kalam and rational disciplines.
[BURHAN:v1p13/r3] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | Although God addressed people in a language they understand and revealed each book in its people’s language, commentary is needed when concise expression hides subtle meaning, premises are omitted, wording permits several readings, or a human text contains errors or omissions.
[BURHAN:v1p13/r4] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | The Qur’an came in clear Arabic among the most eloquent Arabs; they knew its surface meanings and rulings, while subtler meanings emerged through study and, often, questions to the Prophet.
[BURHAN:v2p3/r1] BURHAN, d. 794 · الغزالي | reports | Al-Ghazali and others, followed by al-Razi, give five hundred as the number of legal verses; the author says they likely mean explicit rulings, since stories and parables also yield many rulings, and directs readers to Ibn Abd al-Salam.
[BURHAN:v2p3/r2] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | Legal verses divide into explicit rulings and rulings derived by inference; derived rulings in turn come either from one verse alone or by joining multiple verses.
[BURHAN:v2p3/r5] BURHAN, d. 794 · الشافعي | reports | Al-Shafi‘i infers that ownership automatically frees an ascendant or descendant: servitude is placed opposite parentage, so the two statuses cannot coexist.
[BURHAN:v4p215/r8] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | A second إن functions like ما and enters nominal clauses in an exceptive construction, as in 19:93 and the listed parallel statements. | mentions 6:29, 45:24, 13:7, 2:171, 86:4, 58:2, 19:93, 36:15
